newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine o/night money steady in moderate trade.
newsitem.headline: Philippine o/night money steady in moderate trade.

text.p: * Central Bank keeps overnight borrowing at 10 pct
The Philippine overnight money was steady at 10.03125 percent for the fourth consecutive session as the Central Bank maintained its overnight reverse repo at ten percent, traders said.
"The market was just trading marginally above the Central Bank's floor rate. The system is still awash with cash," one trader said.

Banks had been receiving tax payments from individual taxpayers in the past days, beefing up their peso holdings. Taxes are to be remitted to the Bureau of Internal Revenues after a five-day holding period.
Turnover in the interbank call loan market was moderate with 18.184 billion pesos changing hands within a tight band of 10.03125 percent and 10.25 percent.

The Central Bank raised its three-month special series Treasury bill rates to 9.75 percent from 9.5 percent. However, traders largely ignored the rate adjustment saying the rate was still lower than its corresponding auction rate.
In the secondary market for government securities sellers dominated the market.
"Everybody's trying to sell their T-bills, but there's no aggressive buyer in the market," another trader said. Traders were still expecting rates to inch higher in the coming weeks.
He said banks were buying bills to satisfy their client's needs and not for their own position.
Offer rates for three-month bills were largely soft between 9.90 to 10.165 percent.
